title: Matrix-function actions: exact products and absolute vector error.
summary: Approximate $y^\star=h(A)b$, with the matrix function defined through real-symmetric spectral calculus.

task.description_zh: Approximate $y^\star=h(A)b$, with the matrix function defined through real-symmetric spectral calculus.
description_paragraphs: Approximate $y^\star=h(A)b$, with the matrix function defined through real-symmetric spectral calculus.

model.instance: The unknown real symmetric matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ has spectrum in public interval $[a,\beta]$. The nonzero vector $b\in\mathbb R^d$ and continuous real function $h:[a,\beta]\to\mathbb R$ are public.

assumptions.description: The symmetric matrix spectrum lies in a known interval
The continuous function is public. Scalar computation and polynomial-coefficient selection are free in matrix–vector query units.

model.parameter_domain_description: d>=1, a<=beta with beta>0, epsilon>0, and b nonzero. Retain the current shared parameter domain; A need not be positive definite.
model.description_zh: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ with spectrum in $[a,\beta]$, $a\le\beta$, and the specified $\beta>0$. The public function $h:[a,\beta]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous, with $b\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}$.
description_paragraphs: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ with spectrum in $[a,\beta]$, $a\le\beta$, and the specified $\beta>0$. The public function $h:[a,\beta]\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous, with $b\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}$.

operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact real vector responses, with no observation noise or rounding.

operations.coupling: Every query accesses the same fixed matrix; repeated queries are allowed.
operations.index_control: The algorithm selects vectors and an available channel; block width is charged by column.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^d to R^d, with only the listed right-product channel available. A q-column block costs q calls. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not free additional feedback.
oracle.description_zh: Inputs $d,a,\beta,h,b,\varepsilon$ are public and $A$ hidden. The only hidden-data interface is exact $Av$ at any $v\in\mathbb R^d$. Public scalar-function evaluations and polynomial-coefficient processing are internal work and do not additionally reveal $h(A)b$.
description_paragraphs: The information $d,a,\beta,h,b,\varepsilon$ is public and $A$ is hidden. The only hidden-data interface returns exact $Av$ for any $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Scalar-function evaluation and polynomial-coefficient manipulation for the public function are uncharged internal computations; they do not reveal additional $h(A)b$.

output.allowed_postprocessing: Arbitrary admissible postprocessing; the output need not have appeared as a query vector.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.
output.description_zh: Return any $\widehat y\in\mathbb R^d$, without a Krylov-subspace restriction or additional certificate.
description_paragraphs: Return any $\widehat{y}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, without restriction to a Krylov subspace and without an additional certificate.

metric.normalization: If both numerator and denominator are zero, the loss is zero. A zero denominator with nonzero numerator gives +∞. Otherwise use the stated ratio.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
metric.description_zh: The loss is $\|\widehat y-h(A)b\|_2/\|b\|_2$ and must be at most $\varepsilon$. Continuity on the compact interval ensures that $h(A)$ is finite.
description_paragraphs: The base loss is $\|\widehat{y}-h(A)b\|_2/\|b\|_2$, and success requires it to be at most $\varepsilon$. Continuity on the compact interval ensures that $h(A)$ is finite.

proofs.title: Deterministic evaluation of the best uniform polynomial approximation.
proofs.body: By the definition of r_h(epsilon), choose a public polynomial p of degree r_h(epsilon) with max_{lambda in [a,b]}|p(lambda)-h(lambda)|<=epsilon. The spectral theorem gives ||p(A)b-h(A)b||_2<=epsilon||b||_2. Horner evaluation of p(A)b uses at most r_h(epsilon) exact matrix-vector products. All coefficients and scalar computations depend only on public h and the public spectral interval.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

proofs.title: Deterministic reconstruction using the standard basis, followed by free exact solution of the target task
proofs.body: Recover $A$ using $d$ standard basis queries. Exact internal spectral decomposition and the public scalar function $h$ determine $h(A)b$. The vector error is zero. This uses only the admitted exact-real internal computation and adds no matrix-function oracle.
